steps.say: Everything you can get to lives below, and this box is the quick way in. Type a language and the list narrows as you go.
Tap any one of these and you are straight into it — no setting up, no starting over.
Your current course is not going anywhere. Each one keeps its own place, so you can have a poke at a second language and come back without losing an inch in the first.
steps.terminal: That's the Library. Close it and press play to carry on with the one you are in.

steps.say: Nothing is ever locked behind you. Tap here to open the whole course up.
Every belt is listed, with a tick on the ones you have already come through. Open one and you can look through everything you met there.
Choosing something in there does not just show it to you — it moves you to that point and starts you off from there. So use it when you genuinely want to go over old ground, not to peek.
steps.terminal: If you land somewhere you did not mean to, come straight back in here and pick your way forward again. Nothing is lost by wandering.

walks.title: Hand a class over to another teacher

steps.say: One teacher on a class is the **lead** — the one the class is listed under, and the one a school admin comes to about it. When you move on from a class, that name should move too.
**Make lead** hands it to a colleague already on the class. It takes effect straight away, so add them first and hand over once you have.
Nothing else moves. The pupils, their progress and every session stay exactly where they are, and you stay on the class as a teacher — you have passed the lead, not left.
steps.terminal: That's handover — the lead is a name, not a wall. Nothing changed while you read this; only your own taps do.

walks.title: Put the app on your device

steps.say: **Your account** holds the two things that are about you rather than your organisation: your sign-in, and the app on the device you are holding.

This row already knows what device you are on. On a computer it offers to install the app in its own window; on a phone it offers to add it to your home screen. Same organisation either way — it just saves you finding the tab.
If your browser can do it in one tap, the button does it. If it cannot, the button walks you through your browser's own menu instead — and you can remove the app again any time, like any other app.
steps.terminal: Nothing here is one-time — if you said no on your first visit, this row is still waiting whenever you change your mind.

walks.title: Invite a teacher who isn't here yet

steps.say: Use this when the colleague has no account yet — a supply teacher starting on Monday, or someone new to the school. It saves waiting for an admin to add them first.
**Create a co-teacher link** mints a fresh link the moment you tap it. Whoever opens it lands as a teacher of this class, and of this school — not as its lead, and not over any of your other classes.
Keep it apart from this one. This is the **student** link — anyone who opens it joins the class as a learner. One link makes a colleague, the other makes a pupil, so send them to the right people.
steps.terminal: Short version: the teacher link is minted per colleague and puts them beside you, the student link is the standing one for the class. This tour minted nothing.

steps.say: People join through here — tap **Invite a person**. Nothing is created until you submit the form.

Pick **Group leader** for someone who will run a group of their own, or **Learner** for someone who is here to learn. The link carries the role with it, so they arrive already belonging to this group.
With their name filled in, this mints their own sign-in link — the account exists the moment you tap, and the link IS their login. No sign-up, no password. Send it any way you like.
Every link you mint lands here in **Ways in** — you can revoke it or re-mint it any time. Re-minting kills the old link on the spot.
steps.terminal: That's the whole flow — the link is their login. This tour minted nothing; only your own taps do.

steps.say: People join through here — tap **Invite a person**. Nothing is created until you submit the form.
Pick **Teacher** — the link carries the role with it, so whoever clicks it arrives as a teacher of this school.
With their name filled in, this mints their own sign-in link — the account exists the moment you tap, and the link IS their login. Send it any way you like.
Every link you mint lands here in **Ways in** — you can revoke it or re-mint it any time. Re-minting kills the old link on the spot.
steps.terminal: That's the whole flow — the link is their login. This tour minted nothing; only your own taps do.

steps.say: Three ways to mint access, one form: **Into an organisation** (role links into the tree), **Direct access** (codes and magic links), **New demo org** (a full practice tree).
**Who** silently changes what the submit button does: some options mint a FRESH link, others surface the STANDING link that already exists. Watch the button label switch as you change this.
Every submit on this desk mints REAL access the moment you tap — a leaked leader link makes a stranger a group leader. This tour never taps it for you.
This pill is not just a badge — tapping it is a live kill-switch. It disables or re-enables the link across all four underlying access mechanisms at once.
steps.terminal: Rule of the desk: look before you mint — everything here is live the moment it exists.

walks.title: Move a teacher to another class

steps.say: **Teachers** answers 'who teaches this class?'. A head usually wants the other direction too — 'which classes does this person take?' — and that is the same question read backwards.
**Other classes** on anyone's row asks it that way round. It never moves anybody on its own — it opens a list for you to change.
Every class in the school, with the ones this teacher already takes already ticked. Ticking a second, or a third, is all 'belonging to several classes' means — there is no separate step for it.
A move is just both at once: tick where they are going, untick where they are leaving. You are looking at the truth before you change it, so nothing here is a guess.
Saving applies only the boxes you actually changed. If one of them fails, it says which class failed and why, rather than claiming everything saved.
steps.terminal: That's moving a teacher — one untick, one tick, one save. This tour changed nothing; only your own taps do.

steps.say: The **measure** picks what's being counted — progress, practice, class sessions. The line underneath the pickers says exactly what the current one means.
The **window** is the period the rate is computed over — shorter windows react faster, longer ones smooth the noise.
**Compare to** puts an average alongside. Everything here is a rate, not a raw total — so groups of different sizes compare fairly.
**Overview** takes you back to the same place's home — insights is a lens on where you already are, not a different page to get lost in.
steps.terminal: Rates lead, position is context — and the picker text always says what a measure means.

steps.say: Each card names the language you would be learning, and under it, the language it would be taught in. That second line is the one worth reading — it is what you will hear the prompts in.
The right-hand side tells you where you stand. A coloured dot and a position means you have already started that one and it is holding your place for you.

**Premium** with **Try free** next to it means the course is a paid one, and that you can properly get going in it first. You carry on until the app asks — nothing stops you mid-thought and nothing is taken before you have said yes.
Some languages offer more than one card — a different region or accent of the same language. Pick whichever you would rather end up sounding like.
steps.terminal: Nothing here commits you. Tapping a card takes you into it, and every course you have touched keeps its own place waiting.

steps.say: Students join with this link — share it and they sign up straight into this class.
Prefer a whiteboard? **Show code instead** reveals a standing code — anyone who enters it at saysomethingin.com/redeem joins this class, until the code changes.
**Play as class** is the heart of it: one device — yours — leads the whole class through a session, and it counts for every student on the roster.
steps.terminal: When you're ready, tap Play as class for real — this tour never starts a session for you.

steps.say: Right now everything you have done lives on this device alone. It works perfectly well — but a cleared browser or a new phone takes it with it.
Tap this and you give us an email address, nothing more. We send you a code, you type it in, and your position is yours on any device you sign in on.
steps.terminal: Everything you have already done comes with you — signing in adds your account to it, it never starts you again.

steps.say: **Your account** is your own corner of this page — not the organisation's, yours. Your sign-in and your device live here, and nothing in it is visible to anyone you have invited.
If you arrived through a **link in an email**, that link will not last forever. A password is how you get back into your organisation from a new laptop, a new phone, or after clearing your browser.
Tap **Set a password** and the form opens right here. You will sign in with your email address and that password from then on — and you can come back and change it any time.
steps.terminal: That is the whole thing — one password, always changeable, always in the same place.

walks.title: Share a class with a colleague

steps.say: A class does not have to be yours alone. **Teachers** lists everyone who teaches it, with the lead marked — a job share, a department colleague, a supply teacher covering for a fortnight.
**Add another teacher** is how you share it. Nobody is added until you pick a name and confirm.
You can pick anyone already teaching at your school. If the list is empty, your colleague has not joined the school yet — the link underneath brings them straight in.
What they get is the whole class: the roster, the sessions, the progress, and the right to run a class session. What they do not get is the lead — that stays with you until you hand it over.
steps.terminal: That's sharing a class — same class, two teachers, one lead. This tour added nobody; only your own taps do.

walks.title: Ways in — who can get in, and how to change it

steps.say: Every way in, in one ledger: personal sign-in links and shareable join links, for everywhere below here. Filter by role or by place with the chips.
**Copy** re-shares the same live link — always safe, nothing changes.

**Re-mint** sits on a person's OWN sign-in link, and only there: it makes that person a new link and the old one stops working the moment you tap — if they bookmarked the old one they are locked out until you send them the new one. A shareable link has no Re-mint, because there is nobody to re-bind it to.
**Revoke** switches a link off. It's undoable — a revoked row grows a **Put back** button. For a shareable link this is how you retire it: revoke the old one, then make a fresh one.

And this is where a brand-new shareable link comes from — **Get a shareable link** at the top of this page, one per role. **Invite a person** next to it makes a personal link for someone you can name.
steps.terminal: The short version: copy is safe, revoke can always be undone, re-mint is for one person's own link — and a new shareable link is made at the top of the page, not in the ledger.

steps.say: These are a record of what you have already done. None of them is a target, and none of them is being compared with anybody.
Time is the time you have actually spent learning. If it ever shows a **~** in front of it, that is us working it out from how far along you are, because we have not logged the sessions themselves.
Phrases learnt is how many separate phrases every one of your courses has introduced you to so far. It is added up across all of them, so it grows whichever language you pick up.
steps.terminal: Nothing here changes what you get next. The course follows your position, not these numbers.

walks.title: Where you are in this course

steps.say: This card is your whole position in the course in one glance. Nothing here is a score, and nothing here is counting anything against you.

Those eight coloured dots are **belts**, and the filled one is where you are now. A belt marks how far along the course you have come — it is a position, not a grade, and there is nothing to pass. You move to the next one simply by carrying on.
The bar underneath lays the whole course out end to end, with each belt as its own band of colour. The marker on it is you — so it shows how far you have come rather than how far is left.
Tap the card itself to open the belts up. You can look through everything you have met so far, and start again from any point you fancy revisiting.
steps.terminal: That's your position. Close this whenever you like and press play — it always picks up exactly where you left off.

handbook.title: A question whose page is not built yet
handbook.what: Holding the place of a question that is in the frame but has no page yet, in the same layout as the built ones, so the bar always shows all ten and nothing pretends to measure what it does not.
handbook.where: Any question in the bar shown in the quieter grey.
how: Tap the question in the bar.
Read the card saying nothing is measured for it yet.
handbook.note: This is never a teaser and never a stub with a fake number on it.

handbook.title: Add a class to a group
handbook.what: Creating a class underneath a group you lead, before anyone is teaching it. Useful when you are setting a term up in advance and will put a teacher on each class later.
handbook.where: The group's own page, the **Add a class** button in the row of actions at the top.
how: Open the group the class belongs under.
Tap **Add a class**.
Type the class name.
Choose the course the class will learn.
Tap **Add**.
handbook.note: A class needs no teacher to exist. It sits under the group waiting, and you put a teacher on it whenever you are ready. The course must be one your group has cover for. A paid language you have not subscribed to and are not trialling is refused when you tap **Add**, and the message says so.

handbook.title: Add a school to your programme
handbook.what: Creating a new school inside your programme. The school exists the moment you name it, already attached to your group, with its admin link and teacher link ready to hand over.
handbook.where: All schools, the **+ Add school** button at the top right.
how: Tap **+ Add school**.
Type the school's name and tap **Create school**.
Copy the Admin link and send it to whoever will run the school — opening it takes them straight to sign-in as its admin.
Copy the Teacher link too if you are setting their staff up as well.
Tap **Done**. The new school appears in the list.
handbook.note: There is no separate onboarding step to remember. Both links live on the school's row from then on, so you can fetch them again any time.

handbook.title: Add a school under a group
handbook.what: Creating a school inside a group, so it has its own home page, its own staff and its own learners while still rolling up into whatever sits above it.
handbook.where: The group's home page, **Add a school** along the top.
how: Open the home page of the group the school belongs under.
Tap **Add a school**.
Type the school's name.
Tap **Add**, and the school appears in the list below.
handbook.note: The verb only shows on a plain group. A school cannot contain another school, and an organisation using the neutral wording has groups rather than schools all the way down.

handbook.title: Add a student to a class
handbook.what: Making one learner their own way into one class. The link puts them straight into that class with no forms and no sign-up, so a child can be learning within a minute of opening it.
handbook.where: The class's own page, **Invite students** along the top.
how: Open the class.
Tap **Invite students**.
Type the student's name.
Add their email if you want us to send it, or leave it blank and you get a link to hand over yourself.
Submit, and repeat for the next student.
handbook.note: One student at a time, on purpose — the link is theirs alone and carries the class with it. The **Students** page's **+ Invite students** button brings you here for exactly this reason.

handbook.title: Add a teacher by name
handbook.what: Adding a specific teacher to your school when you know who they are but cannot rely on email reaching them. You type their name and get a code to hand over yourself.
handbook.where: The **Teachers** page, the **Add by name** button at the top.
how: Tap **Add by name**.
Type the teacher's name.
Tap **Create code**.
Read the code out, write it down, or paste it into whatever you already use to reach them.
They go to saysomethingin.app/join and type it in.
handbook.note: They appear on your list straight away under **Not yet given classes**, so you can tick their classes before they have even signed in. The code works once and lasts two days, and whoever uses it becomes that person — so hand it over directly. Made a mistake? Remove them from the list.

handbook.title: Add students to a class
handbook.what: Putting a pupil who is already in your school into this class, for a pupil who has changed set or landed in the wrong class.
handbook.where: The class page, the **Add students** button at the top of the roster.
how: Open the class from **My Classes**.
Tap **Add students** above the roster.
Type a few letters of the name to narrow the list.
Tap the pupil. They appear on the roster straight away.
Add as many as you need, then tap **Done**.
handbook.note: The list holds the pupils in your school who are not in this class yet, and under each name are the classes they are in now, or **In no class**. Adding does not take them out of those classes — a pupil can be in more than one, one for each course they are doing. If you meant to move them, the message that confirms the add names the class they are still in and takes you to it, where their row has a **Remove** button. A pupil brings everything they have already learned with them. For a pupil with no account at all, use the class link in **Invite students** instead.

handbook.title: Bring your first person in
handbook.what: Bringing anyone into this part of the tree — a leader, a teacher or a learner — with a personal link that is their login.
handbook.where: The node's home page, the buttons along the top, **Invite a person**.
how: Open the group, school or organisation you want them to belong to.
Tap **Invite a person**.
Pick the role they arrive as.
Type their name and submit.
Copy the minted link and send it.
handbook.note: Nothing is created until you submit. Every link you mint lands in **Ways in**.

handbook.title: Change how many seats you pay for
handbook.what: Growing or shrinking a live subscription as staff or learners come and go, without going through checkout a second time.
handbook.where: The Upgrade page, once you are already subscribed. The stepper sits beside the running total.
how: Open the Upgrade page.
Step the seat count up or down, or type the number straight in.
The button changes to read Update, with the new monthly total on it.
Tap it. The change is made against your existing subscription — no second charge and no new card details.
handbook.note: While the count matches what you already pay for, the button simply says current and does nothing, so you cannot double-bill yourself by tapping it twice.

handbook.title: Change your school's name and details
handbook.what: Correcting or updating what the app knows about your school — its name, its town, its contact email and a short description. The name is the one that shows on every page your staff and students see.
handbook.where: Settings, then School profile.
how: Open Settings and stay on School profile.
Edit any of the fields — school name, city, region, contact email, about.
Tap **Save changes**. The button reads Saved when it has gone through.
The new name appears across the dashboard straight away.
handbook.note: Only a school admin can edit this. A teacher opening the same page sees the details but cannot change them. Your school's type is set by your group administrator, not here.

handbook.title: Choose what a class learns
handbook.what: Setting the language a class learns. Every class carries one course, and it decides what the class practises, what students hear when they join, and where the class's shared position sits.
handbook.where: The **Create New Class** panel, the **Course / Language** picker.
how: Tap **+ New class** on **My Classes**.
Type into the course box to search the catalogue.
Pick the language the class is learning.
Finish creating the class.
handbook.note: The course is set when the class is made and stays with it. A class that needs a different language is a new class, which keeps the old one's records intact. A school on a free trial is held to the one language it signed up for until it subscribes.

handbook.title: Choose what role someone arrives as
handbook.what: The role you pick on an invite is the role the person lands in, and it travels with the link rather than being set afterwards. Teacher sees their own classes, group leader sees everything below their node, learner just learns.
handbook.where: Any node's home page, **Invite a person**, the role dropdown on the left of the form.
how: Tap **Invite a person** on the node you want them to belong to.
Open the role dropdown.
Pick the role they should hold in this place.
Fill in their name and submit.
handbook.note: The place matters as much as the role — a group leader invited on a group leads that group and everything under it, so invite people on the node whose shape you actually mean.

handbook.title: Choose which courses a school can use
handbook.what: Setting what a school or group is allowed to learn: the whole catalogue when they are paid up, or a named course or two while they are trialling.
handbook.where: The node's home page, **Courses** along the top.
how: Open the home page of the school or group.
Tap **Courses**.
Choose the whole catalogue, or search for the courses the trial should carry.
Save, and everyone below that node inherits it.
handbook.note: A trial runs for thirty days on a paid course and a year on a free or community one, and the server works the dates out on save — what you see before saving is a preview.

handbook.title: Choose which courses your school uses
handbook.what: Narrowing the full list of courses your school can teach down to the handful you actually intend to use, so that choosing a course for a class is a short list rather than a long one.
handbook.where: Step three of first-time setup, the grid of tickable course tiles under **Choose courses**.
how: Open step three of first-time setup.
Everything available to your school starts ticked.
Untick anything you do not plan to teach.
Tap **Continue** — the next step only offers the courses you left ticked.
handbook.note: This is a filter and nothing more. It does not change what your school has access to, and it takes nothing away from anyone. A school on a trial sees its one trial course here; a subscribed school sees the whole catalogue.

handbook.title: Choosing who a question is asked about
handbook.what: Asking the same question of a smaller group: everyone, one course, one organisation or one person. The question does not change; who it is about does.
handbook.where: The map on the left of every question page, the same map the organisation dashboard draws. On a phone it is the first block.
how: Tap **Everyone** to ask the question of every real person.
Tap a course to ask it of that course alone. The other courses stay one tap away as the rows at this level.
Tap **Organisations** to go to the organisation tree and pick a group, a school or a class.
Tap **People** to find one person by name or email.
handbook.note: The choice is written into the page address, so a pasted link opens the same question about the same people.

handbook.title: Claim another email domain for your school
handbook.what: Telling the app which email domains belong to your school, so an arrival using one of them is not pushed to the top of your **Not yet given classes** list as somebody unfamiliar. Your own domain was recorded when you signed up; add the others if your school uses more than one.
handbook.where: Settings, the **Which addresses look like your school** card, the **Add domain** field.
how: Open Settings and find **Which addresses look like your school**.
Type the part of the address after the @, such as example.sch.uk.
Tap **Add domain**.
handbook.note: This grants nothing. Somebody at your domain still sees no learner until you give them a class, and somebody who is not still gets in with one tap. Public providers such as gmail.com or outlook.com cannot be added, because they do not identify a school. Schools in the same trust share each other's domains automatically.

handbook.title: Copy a class link without opening the class
handbook.what: Grabbing a class's join link straight from the class list, for when you are sending links to several classes in one sitting.
handbook.where: **My Classes**, the **Copy link** button in each row.
how: Open **My Classes**.
Find the class's row.
Tap **Copy link**.
Paste it into your email or your lesson slide.
handbook.note: It is the same link the class page offers, so a student who follows it lands in that class either way.

handbook.title: Copy a school's joining links
handbook.what: Fetching the admin link or the teacher link for any school in your programme, so you can chase a school that has not got started or replace a link somebody has lost.
handbook.where: All schools, the Links column on each school's row.
how: Find the school's row in the list.
Tap **Admin** to copy its admin link, or **Teacher** to copy its teacher link.
The chip reads Copied so you know it worked.
Paste it into an email or a message to whoever needs it.
handbook.note: Tapping a link chip does not open the school — the rest of the row does that. A school still flagged as awaiting admin is one whose admin link nobody has opened yet.

handbook.title: Create your first classes
handbook.what: Setting up the classes your school will actually teach. A class is a name, a course and the students who join it, and it is the thing every progress figure in the dashboard is eventually counted against.
handbook.where: Step four of first-time setup, under **Create classes**. **+ Add another class** sits below the rows.
how: Open step four of first-time setup.
Type a class name in the first row. Its course is already set to the language you signed your school up with — change it if this class is learning something else.
Tap **+ Add another class** for each further class; every new row starts on that same language, and fills in the same way.
Remove a row you no longer want with the cross at its end.
Tap **Finish setup** — every filled-in row is created, and each one is marked Added as it saves.
handbook.note: Classes you have already made are listed above the rows, so running the wizard twice will not duplicate them. Students are added from each class's own page whenever you are ready.

handbook.title: Delete a class
handbook.what: Removing a class you no longer want, usually one set up by mistake or a group that has finished. Before anything is deleted the app tells you what goes with it.
handbook.where: The class page, the small bin beside the class name.
how: Open the class from **My Classes**.
Tap the bin next to the name at the top.
Read the list of what will go with the class.
If the class has real practice behind it, type the class name to confirm you mean it.
Confirm the deletion.
handbook.note: Students keep their own accounts and everything they have learned. What goes is the class itself, its roster and its join link.

handbook.title: Delete a school or group
handbook.what: Removing a school or group that should never have existed, or has been wound up. It is the one verb here that takes everything below it with it.
handbook.where: The node's home page, **Delete** at the end of the row of buttons.
how: Open the home page of the school or group.
Tap **Delete**.
Read the summary of what goes with it — classes, people and links are counted for you.
Type the name back when asked, and confirm.
handbook.note: You are only asked to type the name when there is real activity underneath, which is the signal to stop and check. An empty shell deletes on a single confirm.

handbook.title: Delete your school
handbook.what: Closing your school down for good. It removes the school itself along with its classes and everybody's enrolment in them, and it cannot be undone.
handbook.where: Settings, then Data & privacy, at the bottom under Danger zone.
how: Open Settings and choose Data & privacy.
Scroll to Danger zone and tap **Delete school**.
Read what the app lists as going with it — classes, students, teachers and recorded sessions are each counted for you.
If the school has real activity in it, type the school's name exactly to confirm you mean it.
Confirm. You are signed out to a clean slate, because the account you were using belonged to a school that no longer exists.
handbook.note: Only your own school can be deleted this way, and only by its admin. A school with nothing in it deletes without the typed confirmation; one with students and sessions always asks for it.

handbook.title: Download your school's data
handbook.what: Taking your school's progress figures out of the app as a spreadsheet file — every student, the class they are in, how far they have got, how long they have practised and when they were last active.
handbook.where: Settings, then Data & privacy, the button reading **Download all data**.
how: Open Settings and choose Data & privacy.
Tap **Download all data**.
The file lands in your downloads, named after your school and today's date.
Open it in any spreadsheet app to sort, filter or share it.
handbook.note: It is a snapshot of the moment you press the button, not a live link. Download it again whenever you need current figures.

handbook.title: Email someone their invite again
handbook.what: Sending the same invite email a second time to somebody who never found the first one. Nothing changes and no new link is made, so the one they may yet dig out of a spam folder still works.
handbook.where: The node's home page, the **Ways in** section, **Email again** on their row.
how: Scroll to **Ways in** on the node's home page.
Find the person's row.
Tap **Email again**.
The note above the table names the address it went to.
handbook.note: Only rows for a named person with an email on file carry this button. If our mail is being eaten by their school's gateway, read them the link instead of sending it a third time.

handbook.title: Export your class list
handbook.what: Taking the class list away as a spreadsheet, with the name, language, student count, belt, hours this week, sessions, health and join code for every class.
handbook.where: **My Classes**, the **Export CSV** button along the top.
how: Open **My Classes**.
Filter the list down first if you only want part of it.
Tap **Export CSV**.
The file downloads with today's date in its name.
handbook.note: What you export is what you can see, so a filter applied to the table applies to the file as well.

handbook.title: Find a class in a long list
handbook.what: Narrowing a long list down to the classes you care about right now, by language or by how they are doing, and putting them in the order that answers your question.
handbook.where: **My Classes**, the strip of pickers above the table.
how: Open **My Classes**.
Pick a language under **Course** to see only the classes learning it.
Pick a state under **Health** to pull out the classes that need attention.
Change **Sort** to order by students, hours this week or progress.
handbook.note: The totals above the table follow the filter, so the student count and the hours are always the total of what you are actually looking at.

handbook.title: Find out which email you are signed in with
handbook.what: Telling you which email address this account uses, so you never have to guess when you sign in on another device or ask us for help.
handbook.where: **Settings**, at the top of **Account**.
how: Open **Settings**.
Read the address under **You are signed in as**. Tap it to copy it.
Under it is your account code. Tap to copy that too, and give it to us if you ever get in touch.
handbook.note: The account code names your account and nothing more. It does not let anybody in, so it is safe to read out or put in a message.

handbook.title: Finding your way around the organisation
handbook.what: A standing map down the side of every level, showing where you are: the levels above you, the level you are on, its neighbours and what sits under it. It never disappears, so you can always tell how deep into the organisation you have gone.
handbook.where: The column on the left of any group, school or class page.
how: Open any level of your organisation.
Read down the map to see the path from your top level to here.
Tap any name in it to move straight there.
The page rebuilds around the new level and the map redraws with it.
handbook.note: A leader only ever sees their own part of the organisation — the map is trimmed by the server, not hidden in the page.

handbook.title: Give a class its course
handbook.what: Picking the language a class is learning. This is how a course reaches learners at all — a course does not belong to a person, it belongs to a class, and everybody in that class practises it.
handbook.where: On each class row, the course picker beside the class name. It already holds the language you chose when you signed your school up, so most classes need nothing done here.
how: Leave it as it is to teach the language you signed up with.
To teach something else, tap the picker on the class row.
Start typing a language to narrow the list — the catalogue runs to dozens of courses.
Pick the one you want. Where a language offers more than one version, the versions differ by region or accent.
Save the class, and everyone who joins it lands in that course.
handbook.note: The list here is whatever you left ticked at the Choose courses step. If a course you expect is missing, go back a step and tick it.

handbook.title: Give a teacher their classes
handbook.what: Putting a teacher onto the classes they will teach, working from your staff list rather than opening each class in turn. This is how a new arrival gets their timetable in one sitting.
handbook.where: The **Teachers** page, the **Assign to a class** button on that teacher's row.
how: Find the teacher in the list.
Tap **Assign to a class**.
Tick every class they should teach.
Tap **Save** to apply the ticks.
handbook.note: This is also how somebody becomes part of your school. Anyone who used your invite link arrives under **Not yet given classes** and can see no learner at all until you tick a class for them, so a stranger who found the link sits there in plain sight and you can remove them. A class with nobody on it says so in the list, and the teacher you tick will lead it. Tick a class that already has a teacher and yours joins as a co-teacher instead.

handbook.title: Hand a class over to another teacher
handbook.what: Passing the lead of a class to another teacher who already teaches it — for a maternity cover, a term swap, or a permanent handover.
handbook.where: The class page, the **Teachers** section.
how: Open the class from My Classes.
Scroll to **Teachers**.
Find the colleague who should lead it.
Tap **Make lead** on their row.
handbook.note: You stay on the class as a teacher. Only the lead changes.

handbook.title: Hand a teacher their access code
handbook.what: A way to get a teacher into their own account when email is not reaching them. School mail gateways quarantine our sign-in codes often enough that this is the rescue, not the exception.
handbook.where: The **Teachers** page, the **Access code** button on that teacher's row.
how: Find the teacher in the list.
Tap **Access code** on their row.
Read the code out to them, write it down, or paste the link into whatever you already use.
They go to saysomethingin.app/join and type the code in.
Tap **Done** when they are through.
handbook.note: The code works once and lasts two days, and whoever uses it becomes that teacher — so give it to them directly and never post it anywhere shared. Need another? Tap **Access code** again, and the earlier one stops working. This is also how you reissue a code for somebody you added by name who never used the first one.

handbook.title: Hand out a sign-up link for one course
handbook.what: Giving one group of learners a sign-up link that puts them straight into a named course, when your funded year covers more than one. A North Wales tutor hands out the North Welsh link and nobody in that room is asked which Welsh they meant.
handbook.where: The node's home page, the **Ways in** section, the course-named buttons on your sign-up link's row.
how: Scroll to **Ways in** on the node's home page.
Find the row for your sign-up link.
Tap the button named after the course you want, and it is copied.
Send that link to the learners who want that course.
handbook.note: It is the same link and the same cohort either way — the course name only decides where a learner lands. **Copy** still gives you the link that asks them to choose, and everyone gets the whole free year whichever link they came through.

handbook.title: Hand out your staff links
handbook.what: Getting your colleagues in. Your school has a standing teacher link and a standing admin link — send either one and whoever opens it is signed in with that role, with no sign-up form to fill in.
handbook.where: Step two of first-time setup, under **Add your teachers**. The full links are shown as text with a copy button beside each.
how: Open step two of first-time setup.
Copy the **Teacher invite link** for anyone who will run classes.
Copy the **Admin invite link** for anyone who needs to manage the school itself.
Send them however you normally reach staff — email, Teams, a message, or written down.
Anyone who has already joined is listed underneath, so you can see who is in.
handbook.note: A teacher does not need to speak the language. The app does the teaching, so anyone on your staff can run a class.

handbook.title: How every question page is laid out
handbook.what: Every one of the ten questions is answered on a page with the same five parts in the same order, so once you can read one you can read them all: where you are, the answer, the evidence, the rows, and the verbs.
handbook.where: Any page under What's happening.
how: Read the map on the left to see who the question is being asked about.
Read the answer: one plain sentence and one number, with when it was fetched and who is counted directly beneath.
Read the evidence: one chart, never two side by side.
Open any row beneath it. Every row is a link to the thing it names.
The buttons across the top of the main column are the things you can do about the answer. When there is nothing to do, the strip is empty rather than missing.
handbook.note: No page may add a part or move one. A page that tried to would fail the build.

handbook.title: How far a class has travelled
handbook.what: A bar showing where a class has got to in its course, measured in LEGOs — the individual pieces of language the course teaches. The class's own shared position leads, and the average its students have reached on their own sits alongside it.
handbook.where: The **Course journey** card on a class page.
how: Open a class.
Read the bar for how much of the course the class has covered together.
The line underneath gives both figures: the class's shared position, and the average students have reached learning alone.
It also names the next belt and how many LEGOs are left to reach it.
handbook.note: A class that has never played together has no shared position, so the bar falls back to the students' own average and says so.

handbook.title: How fresh these numbers are
handbook.what: A small time stamp saying when the figures on the page were last loaded, so you always know whether you are looking at this morning or this minute.
handbook.where: Just above the row of numbers, reading **Updated** and a time.
how: Open any level of your organisation.
Read the stamp above the numbers for the time they were fetched.
Pull the page down or reload it to fetch again — the stamp moves with it.
handbook.note: Nothing is shown until the first load has genuinely succeeded, so an empty stamp means the numbers have not arrived rather than that they are old.

handbook.title: How many real people practised this week
handbook.what: The first question on a Monday: how many real people practised in the last seven days, and whether that is more or fewer than the seven days before.
handbook.where: **Pulse**, the first question in the bar under What's happening.
how: Read the number and the sentence for this week against last week.
Read the line beneath the chart for how many of those people are paying, gifted or on free access. Gifted people are real people and are counted.
Read the chart for where in the world this week's people are.
Open any course row to see which bits of that course give people trouble.
handbook.note: A person who practised nine times this week counts once.

handbook.title: How students join a class
handbook.what: The one door into a class. A student who follows the class link signs up and lands straight in the class, on the right course, with no code to type. The same class also has a short code for a room where a link is awkward.
handbook.where: The class page, the **Invite students** card.
how: Open the class from **My Classes**.
Copy the link from the **Invite students** card and send it to your students.
For a room with a whiteboard, tap **Show code instead** and write the code up.
Students enter that code at saysomethingin.com/redeem.
handbook.note: The link and the code both stay valid, so the same one works for a student who joins in week one and a student who arrives in week six. If the card says it could not load, do not hand anything out until it comes back.

handbook.title: How your class measures up
handbook.what: A three-bar benchmark on each class, showing the cycles that class has done against the average for your school and the average across everyone learning that course anywhere. It answers the question a total cannot: is this normal.
handbook.where: On each class on the schools dashboard, under the heading naming class, school and global.
how: Open the schools dashboard and find the class you want to read.
The top bar is **Class** — your own class's figure.
**School** underneath it is the average across the other classes in your school.
**Global** is the average across every class doing that course.
Longer bars mean more; the number at the end of each bar is the figure itself.
handbook.note: A class with too little recorded activity shows a dash rather than an invented bar.

handbook.title: Invite a teacher to your school
handbook.what: One standing link that turns anyone who opens it into a teacher of your school. It is the same link every time, so you can hand it to a whole staff room at once.
handbook.where: The **Teachers** page, the **Invite teachers** card below the list.
how: Open **Teachers**.
Scroll to the **Invite teachers** card.
Tap **Copy invite link**.
Send it however you reach your staff — Teams, WhatsApp, printed on a slip.
They open it, sign in once, and appear in your list as a teacher.
handbook.note: If you are standing in front of them rather than sending anything, **Show code instead** gives you a short code to read out or write on a whiteboard, and they type it in at saysomethingin.com/redeem.

handbook.title: Invite a teacher who isn't here yet
handbook.what: Getting a teacher who has no account yet into one class of yours, without going through the school admin.
handbook.where: The class page, the **Teachers** section.
how: Open the class from My Classes.
Scroll to **Teachers**.
Take the co-teacher link.
Send it to them — opening it puts them on this class as a teacher.
handbook.note: The link is scoped to this one class, so a cover teacher never lands in the rest of the school.

handbook.title: Let a named address in through your links
handbook.what: Marking one named person as expected when their email is not at your school's domain: a supply teacher here for a fortnight, or a colleague who only uses a personal address. It stops them being sorted to the top of **Not yet given classes** as somebody you might not know.
handbook.where: Settings, the **Which addresses look like your school** card, the **Add address** field.
how: Open Settings and find **Which addresses look like your school**.
Type their email address exactly as they will use it.
Tap **Add address**, then send them your usual teacher link.
handbook.note: They get in with one tap either way, with or without this. What actually puts somebody in your school is giving them a class. If you know who they are before they arrive, **Add by name** on the Teachers page is the shorter route.

handbook.title: Look up one student
handbook.what: Finding one learner among all of them and opening what they have actually done. The list carries their belt, their hours this week, and when they were last here, so you can often answer the question without opening anything.
handbook.where: The **Students** page, the search box and filters above the list, then **View** on their row.
how: Open **Students**.
Type part of their name in the search box, or narrow the list by class, belt or health.
Read their row for belt, hours and last active.
Tap **View** to open their own progress.
handbook.note: Health is worked out from their last visit and how they sit against their own class, so a learner marked as needing attention is one who has gone quiet or fallen behind the people beside them.

handbook.title: Make a class
handbook.what: Setting up a class of your own: a name, a language, and a link students use to join it. A class holds a roster, its own place on the course, and everything the class practises together.
handbook.where: **My Classes**, the **+ New class** button along the top of the page.
how: Open **My Classes**.
Tap **+ New class**.
Give the class a name you will recognise on a list, such as Year 7 Welsh.
Choose the language the class is learning.
Tap **Create Class**.
handbook.note: The join link is made for you at the same moment. Nothing else is needed to start teaching.

handbook.title: Make a link anyone can use
handbook.what: One link, by role, that you can put in a newsletter or on a slide and let a whole room use. Unlike a personal invite it is not tied to anybody, so new arrivals type their own name before they are in.
handbook.where: The node's home page, **Get a shareable link** along the top.
how: Open the home page of the group, school or organisation they should join.
Tap **Get a shareable link**.
Pick the role everyone using it will arrive as.
Tap **Create invite link** and copy what comes back.
handbook.note: It is open to anyone holding it, so when a link has travelled further than you meant, revoke it in **Ways in** and make a fresh one. Use **Invite a person** instead when you can name who is coming.

handbook.title: Move a teacher to another class
handbook.what: Changing which classes a teacher is on, in one pass, without visiting each class in turn.
handbook.where: The class page, the **Teachers** section, a teacher's other classes.
how: Open a class the teacher is on.
Scroll to **Teachers** and open their other classes.
Tick the classes they should be on and untick the ones they should not.
Save.
handbook.note: Untick and save is how you take a teacher off a class — there is no separate remove.

handbook.title: Name your school
handbook.what: Telling the app what your school is actually called. The name you type here is the one your teachers and students see on every page, on every invite link they open, and at the top of every report.
handbook.where: Step one of first-time setup, the box marked **School name**.
how: Open first-time setup and stay on step one.
Type your school's name as you would write it on a letterhead.
Tap **Continue** — the name is saved before the next step opens.
If you have just arrived and the box is empty for a second, give it a moment and press **Continue** again.
handbook.note: Typing it here counts as confirming it, so you will not be asked to confirm your school's name again afterwards. To change it later, use School profile in Settings.

handbook.title: Open a class
handbook.what: Going from the summary row into the class itself, where the roster, the teachers, the join link and the class's progress all live.
handbook.where: **My Classes**, anywhere on the class's row.
how: Open **My Classes**.
Tap the row for the class you want.
The class page opens on its roster.
handbook.note: The row is a button in its own right, so a keyboard works too. The buttons at the right of the row do their own jobs and do not open the class.

handbook.title: Practice per student per week
handbook.what: Minutes of practice per student per week for this class, set against the same figure for its school and for everyone doing the course. Dividing by students and by weeks is what lets a class of nine and a class of thirty be compared honestly.
handbook.where: The **Practice min/student/week** card on a class page.
how: Open a class.
Read the top bar for this class's own minutes per student per week.
The bars below it are the school average and the global average for the course.
Compare the lengths — the numbers at the end give the exact figures.
handbook.note: A class with too little practice recorded shows a plain line saying so rather than a bar built from almost nothing.

handbook.title: Prove your mailbox reaches you
handbook.what: School mail gateways are ferocious, and a code that never arrives is only discovered on the day you need it. This asks once, at the moment you have just made something worth keeping, and settles it.
handbook.where: A card that appears right after you create a class or copy a class join link, for as long as your address is unproven.
how: Tap **Send me a code**, or nominate a different address if your school one eats our mail.
Type the six digits we send, and tap **That's the one**.
handbook.note: Close it and it stays closed. It never comes back on a timer.

handbook.title: Put the app on your device
handbook.what: Putting SSi on your phone or tablet as an app, so it opens from the home screen and works without a browser tab.
handbook.where: Your node's home page, **Your account**.
how: Open your home page on the device you want it on.
Scroll to **Your account**.
Tap the install row and follow the prompt your device gives you.
handbook.note: Install it on the device you actually teach from — the install belongs to the device, not to your account.

handbook.title: Read your class list
handbook.what: One row per class, showing at a glance how each one is doing: how many students, what belt the class has reached, hours practised this week, the shape of the last seven days, and a health mark for classes worth a look.
handbook.where: **My Classes**, the table filling most of the page.
how: Open **My Classes**.
Read down the health column first, because that is where the app is pointing you.
Use the small chart in each row to see whether practice is steady or has stopped.
Compare hours this week between classes taking the same course.
handbook.note: Health is worked out from how many of the last seven days the class practised on. A quiet week reads as needing eyes, which is a prompt for a word rather than a worry.

handbook.title: Reading one student's progress
handbook.what: Every student in a class, one to a row, each carrying their own position in the course, their belt, their practice over the last week and how recently they were active. A quiet coloured dot flags anyone who has gone quiet or fallen well behind the class.
handbook.where: The **Students** list at the bottom of a class page.
how: Open a class.
Read down the rows — the bar on each is that student's own position in the course, in LEGOs.
The small chart beside it is their practice over the past week, with the minutes named.
The dot and word at the start of a row say whether they are excellent, good, needing attention or inactive.
Tap a row to open that person.
handbook.note: Needing attention means either nothing for a fortnight or less than half the class average, so it is a prompt to look rather than a verdict.

handbook.title: Reading the belts
handbook.what: How a class is spread across the eight belts, from white to black. A belt is earned by completing whole sentences of the course, so it is a coarse, honest badge of distance travelled rather than a score or a grade.
handbook.where: The **Belt distribution** card on a class page.
how: Open a class.
Read the coloured strip for the shape of the class — a wide band of one colour means everyone is together.
The list underneath names each belt and how many students hold it.
The ladder runs white, yellow, orange, green, blue, purple, brown, black, reached at 8, 20, 40, 80, 150, 280 and 400 completed sentences.
handbook.note: Every screen in the product uses that one ladder, so a student never shows a different belt in two places.

handbook.title: Reading your insights
handbook.what: Reading the pace of learning at this level — what is being counted, over what period, and against what.
handbook.where: The node's home page, **See insights**.
how: Open the node's home page and tap **See insights**.
Pick the **measure** — progress, practice, or class sessions. The line underneath says exactly what it means.
Pick the **window** — the period the rate is computed over. Shorter reacts faster, longer smooths the noise.
Use **Compare to** to put an average alongside.
**Overview** takes you back to the same place's home page.
handbook.note: Everything here is a rate, not a raw total, so groups of very different sizes still compare fairly.

handbook.title: Remove a student from a class
handbook.what: Taking a student off a class roster, for a pupil who has changed set or joined the wrong class from a shared link.
handbook.where: The class page, the **Remove** button at the end of the student's row in the roster.
how: Open the class from **My Classes**.
Find the student in the roster.
Tap **Remove** at the end of their row.
Confirm when asked.
handbook.note: The student keeps their account and everything they have learned, and they can join another class straight away. Only their place on this roster goes.

handbook.title: Remove a teacher from your school
handbook.what: Taking a teacher off your school when they leave. Their own account survives — what goes is their place in this school and their view of its classes and learners. It is also how you deal with somebody under **Not yet given classes** you do not recognise, or a name you typed by mistake.
handbook.where: The **Teachers** page, the **Remove** button on that teacher's row.
how: Find the teacher in the list.
Tap **Remove** on their row.
Confirm when asked for their name back.
The list refreshes without them.
handbook.note: An admin's row carries no **Remove** button, so a school can never lose its own admin through this list. Change their role first if that is really what you want.

handbook.title: Rename a class
handbook.what: Changing what a class is called, for a name typed in a hurry or a group that has moved up a year.
handbook.where: The class page, the small pencil beside the class name.
how: Open the class from **My Classes**.
Tap the pencil next to the name at the top.
Type the new name.
Confirm it.
handbook.note: Only the name changes. The roster, the join link, the join code and the class's place on the course all carry on exactly as they were.

handbook.title: Rename a school or group
handbook.what: Changing what a school or group is called everywhere it appears. Nothing else moves — the same people, classes and links carry on under the new name.
handbook.where: The node's home page, **Rename** along the top.
how: Open the home page of the school or group.
Tap **Rename**.
Type the new name.
Tap **Save**.
handbook.note: If the new name matches something else already sitting beside it you are warned and asked to confirm, because two identical names in one list is usually a mistake rather than a plan.

handbook.title: Run your first class session
handbook.what: Running a live practice session with a class in the room, everyone hearing the same thing at the same time.
handbook.where: The class page, the join link and the play button.
how: Open the class from My Classes.
Put the join link or the join code on the screen for the room.
Wait for the students to arrive on their own devices.
Tap play to start the session.
handbook.note: The join code is the same code all lesson, so a student arriving late still gets in.

handbook.title: See and download your funder numbers
handbook.what: The monthly return your funder asks for, on your own page, so you can read it or send it without asking us to pull it.
handbook.where: Your organisation's home page, the **Funder report** section.
how: Open your organisation's home page.
The month shown is the last complete one. Change it to report on another.
Read the three blocks: the month, everything since people enrolled, and the funding year so far.
Tap **Download spreadsheet** to get the same figures as a CSV.
handbook.note: Minutes here are minutes the app was actually speaking to a learner, never time a screen sat open. Somebody who has studied both Welsh dialects is counted once, at their higher dialect, never the two added up. There are no names in this report and there never will be — the age question is a tick precisely so nobody has to hold a birth date.

handbook.title: See every school in your programme
handbook.what: One table of every school you look after, with its students, teachers, classes and practice hours side by side, so a whole programme reads at a glance instead of school by school.
handbook.where: All schools. The totals sit above the table and the search and sort controls sit on its header row.
how: Open All schools.
Read the totals across the top for the programme as a whole.
Search by name to find one school, or sort by name, hours or students.
Read the Status column — a school with nobody running it yet is flagged as awaiting admin.
Tap any row to open that school's own dashboard.
Tap **Export** for the same table as a spreadsheet file.
handbook.note: The list holds still until you refresh it, so a number on screen will not change under you while you are reading. If a refresh fails you are told plainly rather than being shown stale figures as if they were current.

handbook.title: See what a funded organisation gives its learners
handbook.what: Showing the courses an organisation hands out through its own sign-up page, which are given to each learner as they join rather than held on the organisation itself.
handbook.where: The organisation's home page, **Courses** along the top, at the head of the panel.
how: Open the organisation's home page.
Tap **Courses**.
Read the courses listed under the organisation's name, and the length of the free period beside them.
handbook.note: Changing that list is a change to the organisation's enrolment policy, so it is not editable here — everyone who has already signed up keeps what they were given.

handbook.title: See what your school pays
handbook.what: The plain statement of your school's plan — its name, how many teacher seats it is paying for, and whether the subscription is live.
handbook.where: Settings, then Billing.
how: Open Settings and choose Billing.
Read the current plan line: your school, its seat count, and active if the subscription is running.
Tap **Manage subscription & seats** to change how many seats you pay for.
Tap **Billing & invoices** to reach invoices, change the card, or cancel.
handbook.note: Every payment change happens on the one Upgrade page, so there is a single place to go and no second checkout to get confused with. The invoices button appears once a subscription is running.

handbook.title: Set or change your password
handbook.what: Giving yourself a password so you can sign back in without waiting for a link in your email.
handbook.where: Your node's home page, **Your account**.
how: Open your home page and scroll to **Your account**.
Tap the password row.
Type the password you want and save.
handbook.note: Your original invite link keeps working. A password is a second door, not a replacement.

handbook.title: Set up a demo organisation
handbook.what: Standing up a whole organisation with plausible people and activity already in it, for showing somebody what the product looks like once it is running rather than what it looks like empty.
handbook.where: The home page of the node it should sit under, **Mint a demo org** along the top.
how: Open the home page of the node the demo belongs under.
Tap **Mint a demo org**.
Type a name for it, and a leader's email if somebody is to be handed it.
Tap **Mint**, and copy the leader link that comes back.
handbook.note: A demo org's own page grows a **Refresh demo activity** button, which moves its learners on so a demo you minted weeks ago does not look abandoned when you next open it.

handbook.title: Set your language and time zone
handbook.what: Choosing the language the dashboard itself speaks to you in, and the time zone your dates and times are read against.
handbook.where: Settings, then Localisation.
how: Open Settings and choose Localisation.
Pick a **Default interface language**.
Pick a **Time zone** so activity times read correctly for where you are.
Tap **Save changes**.
handbook.note: This is remembered on the device you set it on. Teachers and students each choose their own, so setting it here does not change what anybody else sees.

handbook.title: Share a class with a colleague
handbook.what: Adding another teacher to a class you already run, so you both see the same roster and the same progress.
handbook.where: The class page, the **Teachers** section.
how: Open the class from My Classes.
Scroll to **Teachers**.
Tap **Add a teacher**.
Pick your colleague from the list.
handbook.note: Both of you are teachers of the class. One of you is the lead, and the lead is the one the school's lists show first.

handbook.title: Start a class session from the list
handbook.what: Starting a shared practice session for a class without opening the class first. Your device leads and the whole class moves together from where the class last got to.
handbook.where: **My Classes**, the **Play as class** button at the end of the class's row.
how: Open **My Classes**.
Find the class you are about to teach.
Tap **Play as class** at the end of its row.
The player opens on that class's course, at the class's own place in it.
handbook.note: It is the same session the class page starts, so it moves the class on for everyone on the roster. Only school staff see this button, and only on a live account rather than a read-only view.

handbook.title: Subscribe as a tutor
handbook.what: Paying for your own tutoring dashboard when you teach on your own rather than inside a school. It is one seat, for you.
handbook.where: The **Upgrade** button on your tutoring dashboard.
how: Open the Upgrade page.
Choose Monthly or Annual — annual works out at two months free.
Tap **Subscribe** and fill in the card details on the payment panel that opens on the page.
Once it is running, the same button becomes **Manage subscription** for invoices and cancellation.
handbook.note: Your students pay for their own learning separately, so three paying students cover what your dashboard costs.

handbook.title: Subscribe your organisation
handbook.what: Putting your whole organisation on a paid plan. You pay per learner seat, and one subscription covers every seat and every language across the group.
handbook.where: The **Upgrade** button on your organisation's dashboard.
how: Open the Upgrade page.
Choose Monthly or Annual — annual works out at two months free per seat.
Set the number of learner seats with the stepper. It opens at the number of people already joined.
Tap **Subscribe** and fill in the card details on the payment panel that opens on the page.
handbook.note: A seat belongs to one named learner for the whole period you have paid for, so plan the count against the people you expect rather than swapping seats between them mid-term. You can add more seats at any time.

handbook.title: Subscribe your school
handbook.what: Turning a trial into a paid school. You pay per teacher seat, and one subscription covers every language and every class those teachers run.
handbook.where: The **Upgrade** button on your dashboard, or Settings then Billing then **Subscribe / choose seats**.
how: Open the Upgrade page.
Choose Monthly or Annual — annual works out at two months free per seat.
Set the number of teacher seats with the stepper. It opens at the number of teachers who have actually joined.
Tap **Subscribe** and fill in the card details on the payment panel that opens on the page.
You come back to the dashboard with the subscription live.
handbook.note: Seats are teacher seats, not student seats. Your students do not each need one.

handbook.title: Take a domain or address off your school's list
handbook.what: Taking a domain or a named address off the list your Teachers page sorts by.
handbook.where: Settings, the **Which addresses look like your school** card, the **Remove** button beside the entry.
how: Open Settings and find **Which addresses look like your school**.
Tap **Remove** beside the domain or address.
handbook.note: Nobody loses anything and nobody is kept out. Arrivals from that address simply stop being sorted to the bottom of **Not yet given classes**.

handbook.title: Take a teacher off a class, or move them
handbook.what: Changing which classes a teacher takes without removing them from the school. The ticks start from what is true today, so moving somebody from one class to another is a single change rather than two.
handbook.where: The **Teachers** page, **Assign to a class** on that teacher's row, then the ticks.
how: Open **Assign to a class** on the teacher's row.
Untick the class they are leaving.
Tick the class they are joining, if there is one.
Tap **Save** — the button counts your changes back to you before you commit.
handbook.note: If part of a change fails the panel stays open and names the class it could not do, and the ticks reset to what is actually true. Nothing is ever reported as saved when it was not.

handbook.title: Take your lists away as a spreadsheet
handbook.what: A CSV of whoever is currently on screen, for a report, a governors' meeting, or your own sums in a spreadsheet.
handbook.where: The **Students** page and the **Teachers** page, **Export CSV** along the top.
how: Filter or search the list down to whoever you want.
Tap **Export CSV**.
The file downloads with today's date in its name.
Open it in whatever spreadsheet you use.
handbook.note: The export follows your filters, not the whole school — so a filtered list gives you a filtered file. Clear the filters first if you want everybody.

handbook.title: The class roster
handbook.what: Everyone in the class, one row each, with their belt, how much they have learned, how much they have practised and when they were last at it. This is the answer to who is quietly drifting.
handbook.where: The class page, the **Roster** table.
how: Open the class from **My Classes**.
Read down the mark under each name, which flags anyone behind the class or long gone quiet.
Type a name into the search box to jump to one student.
Compare a student's practice against the class average shown in the rail beside the table.
handbook.note: A student who has never started shows as inactive rather than as behind, because nothing has happened yet to judge. A class nobody has joined yet shows its empty places instead of a table, with **Add students** in it.

handbook.title: The invites desk
handbook.what: The platform-wide desk where SSi mints and manages invites across every organisation at once.
handbook.where: The admin area, **Invites**.
how: Open the invites desk from the admin area.
Pick the mode from the strip along the top — the mode decides what kind of invite you are minting.
Fill in who it is for and submit.
Use the active toggle to read live invites rather than spent ones.
handbook.note: This is the operator's desk, not a school's. A school brings its own people in from its own home page.

handbook.title: The numbers on any level
handbook.what: The row of figures at the top of any level of your organisation. They always count everything below that level, each person once, so a group's numbers already include every school, class and learner underneath it.
handbook.where: Across the top of the page for a group, a school or a class, under the name.
how: Open the level you want — a group, a school or a class.
**Class practice** is the hours classes have practised together beneath this level.
**Classes practising this week** is how many of them have run a session in the last seven days.
**Teachers** and **Learners** count the people below this level, each once however many classes they are in.
On a class the same row switches to that class's own sessions this week, its practice hours, its students and its teachers.
handbook.note: An organisation that is not school-shaped sees the same row worded as practice hours, groups and learners instead.

handbook.title: Voice and pause
handbook.what: What the microphone is actually giving us below this level: how many learners have any mic-derived data at all, and for those who do, how the pause the app leaves them to speak in is settling, and how they sound when they speak.
handbook.where: The **Voice and pause** section at the bottom of any level's insights page.
how: Open a level and tap **See insights**.
Scroll past the rate comparison to the voice section.
Read the uptake figure first — it is how many learners this is based on.
Open a class or a learner within it to see the same reading at a smaller scope.
handbook.note: A learner with no microphone data is absent from these figures rather than counted as a zero, so the denominator is always stated.

handbook.title: Walking down to a school, a class or a person
handbook.what: A drawn tree of everything hanging beneath the level you are on — groups inside groups, the classes in each, the teachers who take them and the staff who teach nothing yet. It is one picture of the shape of your organisation, not a list you have to filter.
handbook.where: The **Below this** panel under the numbers on any group or school page.
how: Open a group or a school.
Tap a caret to open or close what sits under a name.
Tap any name to go to that level — the numbers and the tree redraw for it.
A class row names its teachers and its student count without you opening it.
Where there are more than eight classes or people, a **more** button reveals the rest.
handbook.note: The top two levels open themselves and deeper ones wait to be tapped, so a large organisation shows you its shape instead of eighty-five rows.

handbook.title: Ways in — who can get in, and how to change it
handbook.what: The ledger of every way into this part of the tree — who has a live link, what it lets them do, and how to change your mind.
handbook.where: The node's home page, the **Ways in** section below the lists.
how: Open the node's home page and scroll to **Ways in**.
Read the rows: each one is a live way in, personal or shareable.
**Copy** hands you the link again.
**Re-mint** issues a fresh link and kills the old one on the spot.
**Revoke** closes that way in entirely.
handbook.note: A shareable link is open to anyone who holds it, so revoke is the tool when a link has travelled further than you meant.

handbook.title: When an answer was fetched
handbook.what: Saying when the numbers on a question page were actually read from the database, so you know whether you are looking at this minute or this morning.
handbook.where: Beneath the answer sentence on every question page, reading **Updated** and a time.
how: Read the time beneath the answer.
While it reads **Updating**, the page is still fetching and no number on it is final.
handbook.note: The time is taken when the fetch completed, never when the page drew itself.

handbook.title: When more people join than you have seats
handbook.what: What happens when your school or organisation outgrows the seats it is paying for. Nothing is blocked, nobody is locked out, and no lesson stops. The page simply tells you the truth so you can put it right.
handbook.where: The Upgrade page, the line directly under the seat stepper.
how: Open the Upgrade page.
Read the line under the stepper: how many people have joined, and how many seats are paid for.
If more have joined than you pay for, the line says so and names the difference.
Step the seat count up to match and tap the update button.
handbook.note: This is deliberately an honest count rather than a gate. We would rather show you the gap than shut a class out mid-lesson.

handbook.title: Where the class has got to
handbook.what: How far the class has travelled through its course, as a bar with the class average behind it and the next belt named. A class carries its own place on the course, moved by the sessions you run together.
handbook.where: The class page, the **Course Journey** card in the column beside the roster.
how: Open the class from **My Classes**.
Read the bar for how much of the course the class has covered.
Read the line under it for the class average and how far it is to the next belt.
Compare that with the belt spread underneath, which shows how tightly the class is travelling together.
handbook.note: The class average is the honest number for planning a lesson. The belt spread is the one that tells you whether the class is holding together or pulling apart.

handbook.title: Whether a class is practising together
handbook.what: The headline card on a class: how many sessions it has run this week, how long ago the last one was, and the total hours it has practised together. Classes practising together is what a language programme lives on, so this leads over anything individual students do alone.
handbook.where: The **Class practice** card on a class page.
how: Open a class from the tree or the map.
Read the big figure for sessions run this week.
The line under it gives the time since the last session and the running total of hours and sessions.
handbook.note: A class that has never played together says so plainly and names the teacher's **Play as class** button as the thing that starts the first one.

handbook.title: Which bits of a course make people stumble
handbook.what: Seeing, for one course, which pieces of it real learners skip, retry, or stop on, ranked by how much trouble each piece caused per person who met it.
handbook.where: **Weak points**, under What's happening. Pick a course on the left.
how: Tap a course under **Courses** in the map on the left.
Read the sentence for the piece that gave people the most trouble.
Read the rows, worst first, showing both languages for each piece.
Open a row to see that piece's phrases.
handbook.note: When fewer than five real people have practised a course, the page says **too few to say** rather than showing a number. That is the truth about the course, not a fault in the page.

handbook.title: Who is behind every number
handbook.what: Saying, under every answer, how many real people the numbers on that page are counted from and who has been left out. Demo accounts, SSi staff, class accounts and machine traffic are never counted as people.
handbook.where: The small pill beneath the answer sentence on every question page.
how: Read the pill under the answer for the number of real people counted.
If a page is deliberately showing demo or staff data, the pill says so in red.
handbook.note: The count comes from the server, from one shared rule, never from the page itself. Two pages cannot disagree about who is real.

handbook.title: Why the insights show a rate, not a total
handbook.what: Everything on the insights page is a rate — an amount per learner per week — rather than a running total. A total only ever says how big and how old something is, so a large school always beats a small one. A rate says how fast it is moving, which is the thing you can actually act on.
handbook.where: The comparison block under the pickers on any level's insights page.
how: Open a level and tap **See insights**.
Read the line under the pickers — it says in words what the current measure counts.
The block below puts this level's rate beside whatever you are comparing it to.
Change the window to compute the same rate over a shorter or longer period.
handbook.note: A pace matters more than a position: a class three sentences behind but climbing fast is healthier than one parked far ahead.

handbook.title: Work through setup at your own pace
handbook.what: The first-run wizard that takes a brand-new school from nothing to teachers, courses and classes. It is four short steps and it does not have to be done in one sitting.
handbook.where: Settings, then First-time setup. The steps are listed down the left, and **Save & exit** sits at the bottom of every one.
how: Open the wizard and work down the steps on the left — your school, your staff, your courses, your classes.
**Continue** saves the step you are on and moves you to the next one.
Tap any step in the left-hand list to jump straight to it, forwards or back.
**Save & exit** saves the step you are on and puts you back on your dashboard. If something cannot be saved it stays put and tells you why, so you never leave work behind without knowing.
Come back to Settings and First-time setup whenever you want to carry on.
handbook.note: Nothing here is a one-shot. Everything the wizard sets up — the school name, the invite links, the classes — can also be changed later from Settings and from your class pages. The course ticks on step three are only a filter for the class list on step four, so they are not kept when you leave.

handbook.title: Your class against the average
handbook.what: The teacher's own insight tool: pick one of your classes and see its pace set against the average, over the period and for the measure you choose. It answers whether a class is moving well, which a roster of totals cannot.
handbook.where: **Analytics** in the schools navigation.
how: Open **Analytics**.
Pick the class you want from **Your classes** if you teach more than one.
Pick the **measure** — the line underneath says exactly what it counts.
Pick the **window** the rate is computed over, and what to **compare to**.
Read the comparison block for your class's rate beside that average.
handbook.note: A class with too few sessions to compare honestly says so rather than showing a number built from nothing.

handbook.title: Your classes at a glance
handbook.what: Your teaching dashboard, with your classes first. Every class you teach is a row or a card carrying its course, how many students are in it, their average practice, and the join code you read out to get a new pupil in.
handbook.where: The schools dashboard you land on, above everything else on the page.
how: Open the schools dashboard.
Read down the list — one entry per class you teach.
Tap a class name to open its own page, with the roster and its settings.
**Play as class** on any entry starts a session the whole class does together.
handbook.note: A brand new account shows a single button to create your first class instead of the list.

handbook.title: Your own teaching numbers
handbook.what: One quiet line totalling your whole teaching load — how many students you have across every class, how many hours they have practised between them, and how many sessions have been run. It is a record of what has happened, never a target.
handbook.where: Underneath your classes on the schools dashboard.
how: Open the schools dashboard and scroll past your classes.
**Students** counts every pupil in every class you teach, each person once.
**Hours practised** is real practice time those pupils have logged.
**Sessions** is how many class sessions have been run.
handbook.note: The line only appears once you have at least one class — there is nothing to total before that.
